title: ApprovalDecisionActorV1
description: SPEC-UA-024 (User Resolution Confirmation Contract). Independently authored from 06-policy-approval-governance's own real, checked-in code (services/policy-approval-governance-service GovernanceRequestContext#actorId + infrastructure.identity.JwtIdentityAuthorizationAdapter) rather than imported from anything this service (user-access-authentication-service) itself produces. `sub` is what GovernanceRequestContext#actorId (Authentication#getName()) resolves as decidedBy/requestedBy, and is the exact value JwtIdentityAuthorizationAdapter#isIndependentApprover compares by plain string inequality -- domain 06's own separation-of-duties guarantee depends entirely on this value being stable and non-colliding across resolutions of the same/different real external subjects, never on any call back to domain 01. `iss` must be the same trusted issuer both services validate against. Deliberately does NOT require the `approval:decide` scope value or the `risk_clearance` claim's own contents -- which scopes/claims a token carries is Keycloak/domain-06's own authorization vocabulary, never a condition on domain 01's own JWT acceptance (mirrors SPEC-UA-021's identical domain-boundary reasoning for domain 02).

sub.description: GovernanceRequestContext#actorId reads this directly as Authentication#getName() -- the decidedBy/requestedBy actor for every approval command.

scope.description: JwtIdentityAuthorizationAdapter's own RBAC half reads a SCOPE_* authority derived from this claim; PG's own JwtAuthenticationConverter accepts either shape.

risk_clearance.description: JwtIdentityAuthorizationAdapter's own ABAC half -- a list of RiskLevel names.
